pairs.difference: A: in the lens the bottle is one flat pure-blue mass with almost no neutral steps, set on a fully saturated yellow-orange starburst. Two loud complementary hues fight for attention, and the bottle has no muted resting area. B: a cream map with blue seas sits on muted brown wood planks. It has a believable, quieter palette with more neutral share (subject chroma 0.074). Its hue-family count is high but comes from natural local colors. This is a weak call: neither card is the sci-fi subject.
pairs.fix: Make the plastic bottle a slightly greyed, translucent blue with pale, almost colorless highlights and a darker navy shadow side. Soften the starburst background to a warmer, less saturated yellow so the bottle stands out without both shouting.

pairs.difference: B: the saucer's chrome hull reads in the lens as the same violet as the background (1.26 hue families, warm share 0.02). The only other hue is a ring of orange bulbs, so the card collapses into one hue. A: the orange-yellow player and white earbuds stand out clearly against the purple rings, which is the clear hero-against-background hue split that real cards use.
pairs.fix: Paint the saucer hull a neutral steel grey with a slightly warm light side and a cool blue-grey shadow, rather than tinting it with the purple background. Add one or two more local colors, such as a teal dome or a yellow-orange trim band.

pairs.difference: A: everything is blue: solar panels, starry sky, Earth, and the station's shadows. The lens shows almost a single hue family (1.39) with zero warm share, and background chroma (0.164) is above the real range. The white station body is tinted blue-grey. B: the tiki bar has thatch browns, turquoise water, green stools, and fruit accents, so it has several believable local colors.
pairs.fix: Keep the station's hull a clean warm white with light-grey shading. Make the solar panels a deeper, slightly purple-blue. Calm the space background to a dark, less saturated navy, and add one warm accent, such as gold foil panels or an orange beacon.

pairs.difference: B: the robot's white-grey body comes out cream-yellow in the lens because it takes on the yellow striped wall and orange table (warm share 0.95, subject chroma only 0.026). It has no cool neutral to rest the eye, and its shadow color is pushed warm (1.54). A: the red gloves hold a rich, deep crimson in shadow against a cool blue wall, so hero and background separate.
pairs.fix: Paint the robot body a cool light grey, close to neutral, with blue-grey shadows that do not pick up the yellow wall. Keep the red buttons and antenna tip as the single warm accent.

pairs.difference: A: the rocket's silver body reads in the lens as the same cyan as the sky background, so only cyan and red remain (1.99 hue families, below the real range). The metal has no neutral of its own. B: the yellow submarine has copper portholes, cyan glass, and a grey periscope on dark green, so its local colors are distinct.
pairs.fix: Paint the rocket's metal body a true neutral silver-grey with a warm light side and a slate-grey shadow, not a cyan tint. Add one more local color, such as a white band or a yellow flame.

pairs.difference: A: the teal console's shadow side goes dark and greyed (shadow chroma kept 0.65, at the bottom of the real range), and the red buttons read orange-brown in the lens. The orange floor reflects back into the base. B: the blue vending machine keeps saturated blue in shadow against magenta-purple, and the colored cans make a clean palette. This is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Keep the console's shadow side a rich deep teal instead of muddy grey. Make the buttons a clear cherry red with darker red undersides, and keep the orange background from bleeding onto the base.

pairs.difference: B: the whole lab, including floor, walls, chrome pod, and console, is one violet-lavender family with cyan glow trim and orange bulb accents. The pod's metal is tinted purple, not neutral. A: the red bus has blue sky, cream clouds, pink buildings, and a grey road, giving many natural local colors (6.3 families).
pairs.fix: Make the pod's shell a neutral brushed steel with a faint warm highlight. Give the room at least one non-violet surface, such as a dark grey-blue floor, so the purple stays as background only.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is a single pure, maximum red (subject chroma 0.217, above the real range) with almost no shift toward deeper crimson in its folds, set on loud cyan. B: the teal book on warm wood with multicolored stickers has more muted wood mass to rest the eye. This is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Paint the scarf a slightly deeper, less neon red, with wine-red shadows in the folds and softer pinkish-red highlights. Keep the gold badge as the only accent.

pairs.difference: A: in the lens the planet is one orange-red mass, and the magenta band and cream ring both read grey-green. They are tints with little body of their own, so the hero is a near-pure orange ball on cyan. B: the yellow fins with purple foot pockets on violet use a deliberate yellow/purple split, and the dark grey blades give a neutral rest.
pairs.fix: Give the planet richer bands with real color: a deep magenta stripe and a darker rust-red shadow side. Make the ring a warm sand color with its own soft grey shadow.

pairs.difference: A: the moon ground, wheels, and rover frame are all a flat warm grey. Subject and background chroma (0.056 and 0.069) are below the real range, and shadows lose almost all color (shadow chroma kept 0.25). Only the orange deck and blue sky carry color. B: the wooden boat and dock on turquoise water keep rich orange-brown shadows.
pairs.fix: Tint the lunar ground a cool blue-grey with slightly purple crater shadows. Make the rover's shadow side a deep warm brown-orange rather than dead grey. Raise the orange deck and the sky so they read as clear color masses.

pairs.difference: A: the helmet's white shell comes out cream-peach in the lens, the visor is the same orange as the burst background, and warm share is 0.98. The whole card is pulled into one orange family, and only a thin blue stripe breaks it. B: the khaki jacket, orange collar, and green sash sit on a green burst, a balanced warm-hero/cool-background split.
pairs.fix: Paint the helmet shell a clean cool white with light blue-grey shading. Make the visor a reflective gold that is darker and browner than the background. Widen the blue trim so it reads as a real color, or change the background to a cooler color.

pairs.difference: A is the real computer card from the lessons: neutral grey-white plastic against an orange gradient and a brown desk. B: the lime alien is set on hot pink, and the metal floor in the lens turns pink-violet and olive. Its neutrals are taken over by the two loud complementary hues, and pink spots repeat the background on the hero.
pairs.fix: Make the metal floor a neutral cool grey with darker blue-grey shadows that do not pick up the pink wall. Calm the backdrop to a softer, dustier rose, and keep the alien's spots a darker coral rather than the same pink as the wall.

pattern: On generated cards, neutral materials (white plastic, chrome, steel, grey ground) do not stay neutral. They get tinted by the background hue: cream or peach on orange cards, violet on purple, cyan on blue. The card then collapses into one or two hue families, with the hero repeating the background color. When shadows aren't dulled to grey, they shift toward the background color. Real cards keep cool-grey whites, distinct local colors for each part, and a clear hero-versus-background hue split.
